title: BBV pulls off mammoth HS2 M42 bridge treble
content: Balfour Beatty Vinci has completed a mammoth weekend engineering operation on HS2, dropping the final two 1,000-tonne viaduct spans into place over the M42 near Birmingham. The contractor also finished installing the 175 beams forming the roof of a second major bridge three miles away, bringing four weekends of intensive motorway works to a close. The latest operation saw a 75-strong team install two 45m-long spans at Water Orton, completing all six viaduct crossings over the motorway. How HS2 Water Orton twin viaduct crossing will look Each span was assembled from 18 precast concrete segments manufactured at BBV’s Kingsbury batching plant before being driven into position on self-propelled modular transporters and locked together using internal tensioning cables. Meanwhile, a separate 150-strong team installed the final 44 beams on the 300m-long M42 twin box near the NEC. M42 twin box under construction A 300-tonne crawler crane lifted the 23m-long beams, weighing up to 92 tonnes each, into position to complete the structure’s 9,800-tonne roof. The twin box now stands 10m high, supported by two 145m-long walls and 46 internal columns. CGI of completed box structure carrying HS2 over M42 Both operations were completed during a weekend motorway shutdown, with the M42 reopening at around 4am on Monday, an hour ahead of schedule. Click for video BBV project director Oliver Shore said: “This was a huge engineering challenge and I’m so proud of the way our teams have responded. ” The two Water Orton viaducts form part of HS2’s triangular delta junction, linking Birmingham with the main line heading north. BBV will now extend Water Orton 2 by another 40m to close the final gap over Gilson Road. The M42 will shut again from 23 to 26 October to allow the contractor to install parapets above the motorway.
